report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward culinary/recipe/restaurant content (and a somewhat “professional/instructional” tone), relative to Model A.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are dominated by cooking/food/restaurant terms across many layers and positions: “Cook/Hot/pot/pepper,” “cooking/Cooking/baking/Cake/microwave/oven/kitchen,” “Restaurant/Chef/Professional,” “culinary,” “Chef,” “Kitchen,” recurring strongly from layers ~19–25 at positions 1–4. Examples: L21–L25 pos1–4 repeatedly list “Cooking/cooking/baking/restaurant/Chef/Professional/kitchen/Cake.”
- Earlier mid-layer cells show formal/academic-ish vocabulary (“dissertation,” “Innovation,” “sciences,” “copyrighted,” “metropolitan”), but this consolidates in later layers into a very specific culinary cluster, suggesting the net effect of B−A steers predictions toward food/recipe/restaurant discourse.
- The difference norm is concentrated in later layers, especially at pos1 (e.g., layers 20–25), indicating a strong, early-in-sequence topic/style prior rather than a narrow lexical quirk.

Caveat:
- Patchscope samples were not provided, so we can’t show direct generations; however, the consistency and dominance of culinary tokens across many top-norm cells support a specific domain tilt toward cooking/recipes/restaurants.
